A narrower reading would keep the cell at same because the downstream readouts did move; it was rejected because the readouts that moved are the GLP-1R ones. PET trial NCT03350191 has no posted results, so registry_date is null and the year is the 2020-10-07 online date.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; no exposure target for humans is stated.

dose.note: At SAR425899's top phase-2 dose 6 of 13 patients stopped for adverse events and glucagon-receptor occupancy was 11 %: the mouse-tolerated dual exposure was unreachable. SAR425899 track; the cotadutide and efinopegdutide GI ceilings in the judgement are context, not scored here.

dose.quote: Six out of 13 included patients prematurely discontinued the study due to adverse events.

dose.reason: Glucagon-active exposure not tolerated in patients
dose.judgement: Decision 16 call: the model stated the effective exposure was tolerated (margin_stated true), and in patients the dose stopped at a GI-tolerability ceiling (0.2 mg/day SAR425899; 300 ug/day cotadutide; 26 % of JNJ-64565111 recipients did not complete 12 weeks) at which the glucagon receptor was not measurably occupied, so the dual-agonist exposure the mouse worked at was never reached: contra with blocked_by toxicity. Not derived from efficacy, because the GLP-1R-driven primary endpoints were met at these doses. The alternative is untested on the ground that GI intolerance is a harm the mouse cannot show, so no real margin was stated; it was set aside because the brief scores the stated margin, not the species' capacity. Paired by the drafter; Day 2009 is the model side.
dose.magnitude_basis: GCGR occupancy 11.2 % at the maximum tolerated phase-2 dose; no human exposure target was stated by the model

efficacy.judgement: Same, not contra, because every member's primary endpoint responded in the predicted direction vs placebo: cotadutide HbA1c -0.83 to -1.04 % and weight -2.0 to -3.6 % at 14 weeks (NCT03235050), SAR425899 HbA1c -0.85 to -0.96 % (NCT02973321), LY2944876 HbA1c -0.78 to -1.15 % (NCT02119819), OPK-88003 HbA1c -1.47 vs -0.25 % (NCT03406377), MK-8521 300 ug HbA1c -0.61 % (p=0.018; the 180 ug arm missed, p=0.126), JNJ-64565111 weight -4.6 to -7.2 % (NCT03586830). Called partial because the mouse's specific prediction, superior weight loss with equal glucose control against a GLP-1R agonist, mostly did not hold: cotadutide 300 ug beat liraglutide 1.8 mg on weight at 14 weeks (-0.93 %, p=0.042) but not at 54 (p=0.357); MK-8521 300 ug equalled liraglutide on weight (-0.2 kg, p=0.81) and 180 ug was inferior on HbA1c (+0.60 %, p=0.017); SAR425899 equalled liraglutide on both; LY2944876 10 and 15 mg were inferior to exenatide ER on HbA1c; JNJ-64565111 produced no HbA1c change and higher fasting glucose in T2D. The stricter reading (model prediction = dual beats mono, so contra) was rejected because the primary endpoints were placebo comparisons and were met. Registry results for NCT02548585 posted 2019-04-05, after the 2018-06-23 online date.

efficacy.note: SAR425899 for 28 days lowered fasting plasma glucose and weight in overweight/obese T2D patients (NCT02411825), as the obese diabetic monkey predicted; direction only, no comparator arm. Retrodiction: this model result (Elvert 2018, monkey surrogate, received 2017-05, online 2018-01) was first public after Transition Therapeutics' 2013-04-30 release of the pegapamodutide (TT-401) five-week T2D study, fasting glucose and weight down vs placebo; for engagement and efficacy any drug's earlier patient result for the target counts. Settles the rule question on the sponsor's internal MAD readout: moot, because a public class patient result already predated the model.
efficacy.short: Glucose and weight fell in dosed T2D patients
efficacy.quote: SAR425899 was well tolerated and led to favourable glycaemic effects in patients with T2D and weight reduction in both healthy volunteers and patients.
efficacy.confidence_note: Patient side abstract-level; NCT02411825 has no posted results, so registry_date is null. Model side full text but a surrogate peptide, not SAR425899.
efficacy.reason: Glucose and weight fell as in the monkey
efficacy.judgement: Monkey predicted glucose and weight lowering in obese diabetic primates; Tillner 2019 reports both in T2D patients after 28 days. Same, direction only. Dated by the 2018-09-16 online date.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of fasting glucose and weight in T2D patients; monkey effect sizes not ratioed (surrogate peptide)

efficacy.model: Obese diabetic cynomolgus monkey (chronic dosing, monkey-specific surrogate of SAR425899, liraglutide comparator)
efficacy.note: 26-week phase 2 (NCT02973321): HbA1c -1.5 to -1.6 % vs -0.66 % placebo and -1.31 % liraglutide, the monkey's glucose match held; weight -4.3 to -5.3 kg vs -4.6 kg liraglutide, so the weight edge did not follow. Retrodiction: this model result (Elvert 2018, monkey surrogate, received 2017-05, online 2018-01) was first public after Transition Therapeutics' 2013-04-30 release of the pegapamodutide (TT-401) five-week T2D study, fasting glucose and weight down vs placebo; for engagement and efficacy any drug's earlier patient result for the target counts. Settles the rule question on the sponsor's internal MAD readout: moot, because a public class patient result already predated the model.
efficacy.short: HbA1c met; no weight edge over liraglutide
efficacy.quote: SAR425899 and liraglutide improved postprandial glucose control in overweight to obese subjects with T2D.
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results (posted 2021-02-09) read directly for HbA1c and weight; Schiavon 2021 is the MMTT sub-analysis. Model side full text, surrogate peptide.
efficacy.reason: Glucose translated; weight edge over liraglutide did not
efficacy.judgement: Primary HbA1c met vs placebo and no worse than liraglutide, as the monkey predicted: same, direction only. The 'greater effects on body weight' than liraglutide failed in patients, but under #80 a comparator-ranking miss is untested and does not change status; recorded here. Dated by the registry posting. Strengthens the 2018 same: a 26-week randomised trial with a registry-posted HbA1c primary replaces a 28-day abstract-level signal.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of HbA1c and weight vs placebo; monkey surrogate effect sizes not ratioed

patient_trials.quote: SAR425899 and liraglutide improved postprandial glucose control in overweight to obese subjects with T2D.

safety.note: Mouse papers report no overt adverse effects. Patients showed GI intolerance (not mouse-visible) and MK-8521 raised heart rate 7 bpm vs placebo; no source compares. Ruling: the passing claim of no overt adverse effects is a safety prediction of the model, scored on the SAR425899 track (appended entry).
safety.quote: These preclinical studies indicate that when full GLP-1 agonism is augmented with an appropriate degree of glucagon receptor activation, body fat reduction can be substantially enhanced without any overt adverse effects.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Henderson 2016 also dosed healthy cynomolgus monkeys for 2 months; its abstract is silent on emesis and heart rate.
safety.reason: No admissible comparison; harms listed in note
safety.judgement: Left untested rather than contra. The candidate miss is heart rate: MK-8521 raised it 6.9 and 7.7 bpm vs placebo and 3.8 and 4.7 bpm vs liraglutide at week 12 (NCT02492763, a pre-specified primary safety outcome), a harm a mouse or monkey could show, but the only record is a registry table with no quotable sentence and the model papers' abstracts do not mention heart rate, so the silence cannot be verified at abstract level. Nausea and vomiting (higher than placebo and liraglutide with JNJ-64565111; the discontinuations in Eriksson 2020) are not mouse-visible and are already counted in dose. GLP-1R-agonist class harms (C-cell tumours, pancreatitis) belong to another drug class and are set aside under decision 13; no member reached carcinogenicity testing.

safety.model: Healthy cynomolgus monkey (4- and 8-week repeat-dose toxicology studies, cotadutide)
safety.note: Cotadutide-dosed monkeys, a species that vomits, showed no adverse clinical signs or vomiting at 8-27 nmol/kg/d; one 27 nmol/kg animal was killed for weight loss.
safety.short: No vomiting or clinical signs in monkeys
safety.quote: Bodyweight loss was not associated with any adverse clinical signs or vomiting in monkeys
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5129521); quote is the opening clause of a longer sentence that goes on to describe one female at 27 nmol/kg/d killed on day 36 for poor clinical condition attributed to ~20 % weight loss.
safety.judgement: Opening untested entry. Unlike the DIO mouse, the monkey can show emesis, so this is a stated negative safety prediction in a capable species; the same paper also calls the receptor balance 'optimal for both glycaemic control and safety'.

safety.model: Healthy cynomolgus monkey (4- and 8-week repeat-dose toxicology studies, cotadutide)
safety.note: Phase 2a: GI disorders in 72 % of cotadutide patients vs 40 % on placebo, 3 of 25 stopped for adverse events; monkeys showed none.
safety.short: Monkeys clean; 72 % GI disorders in patients
safety.quote: gastrointestinal disorders (18 [72%] vs 13 [40%]) and decreased appetite (five [20%] vs none) occurred more frequently with MEDI0382 than placebo.
safety.confidence_note: Patient side abstract-level (PubMed abstract via efetch; Lancet paywalled), which gives GI disorders as a group, not vomiting alone; the vomiting rate comes in the 2020 strengthening entry. Model side full text.
safety.judgement: Paired by the drafter: Henderson 2016 stated, for cotadutide itself in a species that can vomit, that weight loss 'was not associated with any adverse clinical signs or vomiting'; Ambery 2018 found GI disorders in 72 % vs 40 % and all four phase 2a discontinuations were for adverse events. A stated prediction of no GI harm in a capable species, contradicted in patients, is contra on this track (the dio-mouse track stays untested on this harm because a mouse cannot vomit, and the GI dose ceiling is already counted in that track's dose cell). The monkey toxicology doses were far above the clinical dose, which makes the miss worse, not better. Not 'opposite' in magnitude: that term is for a predicted harm that never appeared; here the model predicted absence. Registry results (NCT02548585) posted 2019-04-05, after the 2018-06-23 online date.
safety.magnitude_basis: GI disorders 72 % vs 40 % placebo (phase 2a, n=25 vs 26) against a stated absence of adverse clinical signs or vomiting in monkeys at 30-100 ug/kg/d; no rate to ratio

safety.model: Healthy cynomolgus monkey (4- and 8-week repeat-dose toxicology studies, cotadutide)
safety.note: 54-week phase 2b (n=834): nausea 35 % and vomiting 17 % with cotadutide, more than placebo or liraglutide. Vomiting itself, the harm the monkey denied.
safety.quote: The most common adverse events with cotadutide (nausea, 35%; vomiting, 17%) decreased over time.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC8247525). Vomiting rate is pooled across 100-300 ug doses; the paper also states cotadutide had more GI disorders than placebo and liraglutide.
safety.judgement: Strengthens the 2018 contra with the specific harm the monkey study named. Year 2020 because the trial's registry results (NCT03235050) posted 2020-07-20, before the 2021-05-20 online publication that carries the quotable sentence (rule 6: earliest public date); the registry AE table lists vomiting counts but no sentence.
safety.magnitude_basis: vomiting 17 %, nausea 35 % of cotadutide-treated T2D patients over 54 weeks vs none stated in monkeys; no rate to ratio

safety.note: Ruling: the DIO mouse's passing claim of no overt adverse effects is a safety prediction. SAR425899 was well tolerated in T2D patients over 28 days; GI intolerance, not mouse-visible, is counted once in dose.
safety.short: Mouse tolerability claim held in T2D MAD
safety.quote: SAR425899 was well tolerated and led to favourable glycaemic effects in patients with T2D and weight reduction in both healthy volunteers and patients.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level on both sides. Day 2009 dosed a sibling PEGylated co-agonist, not SAR425899. Later SAR425899 studies stopped patients for GI adverse events (Eriksson 2020), a harm the mouse cannot show, scored in dose not here.
safety.reason: Tolerability claim held for mouse-visible harms
safety.judgement: Ruling 2026-11-09: a statement that the drug was well tolerated, even in an efficacy paper, is a safety prediction. Paired by the drafter: Day 2009 is the model side; Tillner 2019 the patient side. Same, partial, because tolerability held on mouse-visible harms while GI intolerance (not mouse-visible) capped the dose and is counted in the dose cell. Prospective: no SAR425899 patient result predated Day 2009.
safety.magnitude_basis: presence vs absence of adverse effects
safety.population: Overweight/obese adults with type 2 diabetes (28-day MAD)
